description: A picture of a scene as the editor's 2D or 3D view draws it, including what its @tool scripts draw under Engine.is_editor_hint(). No game and no headless engine runs that branch, so runtime_capture cannot show it. The editor opens the scene, shows its 2D or 3D view for a few frames and captures it. It then returns to the scene and view it showed before, and closes the scene again if it was not open. The view is the editor's own, at its zoom and scroll for that scene, and in 3D with its grid and gizmos. A scene open with unsaved changes is captured as the editor holds it. Other calls to the editor wait for the capture. Needs a connected editor that draws: a visible one, or a hidden one on Windows. A hidden editor on Linux or macOS is headless and is refused. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

height.description: Scale the picture to this height. Given alone, the width keeps the picture's proportions.

inline.description: Send the picture back in the answer. Default true, as a JPEG when that is smaller than the PNG and the picture has no transparency. false sends none and needs outputPath.

outputPath.description: Also save the picture as a lossless PNG at this absolute path. The answer says where. Refused unless it ends in .png, its directory exists, it is outside the project, and no file is there already.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

scenePath.description: Scene file inside the project, such as "scenes/main.tscn" or "res://scenes/main.tscn".

view.description: Which of the editor's views draws the scene. Default 3d for a scene whose root is a Node3D, and 2d otherwise.

width.description: Scale the picture to this width. Given alone, the height keeps the picture's proportions.

name: editor_capture
title: Capture the editor's view of a scene
